title: Scheduled Task Created Through PowerShell
detection_hypothesis: If persistence is created programmatically, the logged script block will contain a scheduled task registration cmdlet together with an action definition.

field_semantics.ScriptBlockText: Decoded PowerShell script block text as executed.

collection_prerequisites: Script block logging is enabled through Group Policy or registry configuration.
PowerShell operational log collection is enabled on the endpoint.
expected_collection_gaps: PowerShell version 2 engines do not emit script block logs.
Very large script blocks are split across multiple events.
normalization_assumptions: ScriptBlockText contains the decoded script text as executed.
ingestion_differences: Multi-part script blocks may need reassembly before matching.
Some pipelines strip newlines from ScriptBlockText.
retention_considerations: Script block logging is moderate to high volume; 90 days is a common target.
false_positive_strategy: Benign matches dominate this rule, which is why it is low severity. Tune by enriching with the task action path and by hunting on tasks whose action points at a user-writable directory.
tuning_guidance: Combine with the temporary path scheduled task rule instead of excluding configuration management modules, so that unusual task actions remain visible.
test_strategy: Positive cases register a task with an action object and with an inline action parameter. Negative cases query tasks, unregister a task, and mention the cmdlet name in a comment.
author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
